'''Kay Kinoshita''' is an experimental [[particle physicist]]. She is a professor at [[University of Cincinnati]].

Kinoshita completed her undergraduate studies in physics at [[Harvard University]] in 1976 and her PhD at [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://homepages.uc.edu/~kinoshky/vita.html|title=Kay Kinoshita|website=homepages.uc.edu}}</ref> She then returned to work at Harvard, before becoming a full professor at [[Virginia Tech]] in 1993.

She is currently a professor at [[University of Cincinnati]] and was head of the Physics department 2009-2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://engage.aps.org/fdi/governance/executive-committee/biographies|title=Governance - Unit - FDI|website=engage.aps.org}}</ref> She is investigating topics such as [[dark matter]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2020-07-physicists-celebrate-japan-collider.html|title=Physicists celebrate Japan collider record|first1=Michael|last1=Miller|website=phys.org|date=16 July 2020}}</ref>

She was a 2020 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] for "innovative contributions to the study of b-quarks and for leadership in accelerator searches for magnetic monopoles."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org}}</ref>
